elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted Ownership section: "The Company owns all right, title and interest in the Site and in all deliverables and work product created for the Company under this Agreement".

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: "...and HDI hereby assigns the same to the Company" — present-tense assignment of the Site, deliverables and work product to the Company.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "HDI retains its pre-existing intellectual property..." — express carve-out for HDI background IP, consistent with the Company ownership sentence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "...grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license to any HDI intellectual property embedded in such deliverables."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: "The Company retains all rights in all Content, user information and other data belonging to, supplied by, or collected or processed for the Company (\"Company Data\")" — retention of all rights over every category of Company data.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "...any license to HDI in Company Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services under this Agreement" — no distribution, resale, independent-exploitation, consent-based or "purposes contemplated" widening is retained anywhere; Section 8.1 only imposes confidentiality obligations on HDI and grants no use rights.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: "No intellectual property shall be jointly owned by the Parties." Section 10.2's "co-ownership" language concerns the parties' business relationship, not IP, so no contradiction.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: "HDI retains its pre-existing intellectual property" preserves HDI's background tools and know-how, subject only to the embedded-IP licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The perpetual licence runs only to "HDI intellectual property embedded in such deliverables"; there is no separate licence to the Deliverables themselves (the Company owns them outright, so the fallback licence construct is absent).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence exists in the inserted text — only an embedded-IP licence; the irrevocability modifier is not attached to a Deliverables grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence, and the embedded-IP licence omits any territorial term ("worldwide" does not appear).

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Royalty-free applies only to the embedded HDI IP licence; there is no Deliverables licence to which it attaches.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No express use-and-modify licence language; the clause relies on outright Company ownership instead of the fallback licence rights.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right is stated for the Deliverables or the embedded HDI IP.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "...any license to HDI in Company Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the services under this Agreement".

reasons: The rule is correctly classified as missing: the Agreement had no IP or data ownership provision. Sections 2.1, 5.2, 6.1 and 8.1 address Content delivery, editorial control, a limited trademark licence and confidentiality, none of which allocate ownership of the Site, deliverables or Company data.

All nine preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted Ownership section: Company ownership plus a present-tense HDI assignment, HDI's retained pre-existing IP with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded HDI IP, Company retention of all rights in a broadly defined Company Data (data belonging to, supplied by, or collected or processed for the Company), an HDI data licence limited solely to providing the services, and an express no-joint-ownership sentence.
The fallback level is incomplete (no worldwide, use/modify or sublicense rights, and no Deliverables licence construct), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletions or paraphrase of surrounding text, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural boilerplate, and no duplicated operative terms. The reference to "the Site" is not an extra because the Site is the deliverable HDI develops under Sections 1.1-1.3.

Intent is preserved: the trademark licence in Section 6.1, the confidentiality regime in Section 8.1, the Company's editorial control in Section 5.2 and HDI's hosting obligations all survive without contradiction; the no-joint-ownership sentence is confined to intellectual property and so does not disturb Section 10.2's relationship language. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and "Company Data" is defined in the inserted text.
Drafting nit only (not a defect in coverage): the inserted section carries the heading "Ownership." without a section number — number it in line with the Agreement's scheme before sending.
